workflow_details.description: Add information that will help to differentiate this workflow from another.
workflow_details.title: Workflow Details

data_source.description: Select one of your configured data sources.

time_range.description: Choose the period of time to analyze.
time_range.title: Time Range

subject_group_name.title: Subject Group Name
subject_group_name.description: The EarthRanger subject group to animate, picked from the chosen data source's subject groups. ⚠️ The use of a group with mixed subtypes could lead to unexpected results.

include_subject_additional.title: Include Subject Additional
include_subject_additional.description: Whether or not to include the subject's free-form `additional` JSON

subject_observations.title: Subject Group
subject_observations.description: Choose the subject group whose movements will be animated. Each subject in the group is drawn as its own track.

trajectory_segment_filter.description: Filter track data by setting limits on track segment length, duration, and speed. Segments outside these bounds are removed, reducing noise and to focus on meaningful movement patterns.

convert_to_trajs.title: Trajectory Segment Filter
convert_to_trajs.description: Clean the tracks before animating by removing segments that are too long, too short, too slow or too fast to be real movement, such as GPS jumps.

Terrain.description: Control how the 3D terrain looks and how tracks sit on it.

exaggeration.title: Exaggeration
exaggeration.description: Vertical exaggeration factor. 1.0 = true scale, 2.0 = 2x heights.

terrain_exaggeration.title: Terrain Exaggeration
terrain_exaggeration.description: Control how strongly hills and valleys are raised on the 3D terrain. Increase it to make relief easier to see in flat landscapes.

altitude_mode.title: Altitude Mode
altitude_mode.description: Height of the tracks: on the ground (clamp_to_ground; lines can dip into the terrain between fixes), `offset` metres above it (relative_to_ground), or each fix's recorded altitude above sea level (absolute).

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Metres above the ground (relative_to_ground), or above sea level for fixes without an altitude (absolute). Ignored by clamp_to_ground.

ground_elevation.title: Ground Elevation
ground_elevation.description: Constant ground used only if DEM sampling fails.

terrain_sampling.title: Terrain Sampling
terrain_sampling.description: Control how tracks are draped onto the 3D terrain so they sit on the ground surface rather than floating above it or disappearing below it.

texture.title: Basemap
texture.description: Map imagery draped over the terrain in the interactive map and the video.

terrain_layer.title: Basemap
terrain_layer.description: Choose the basemap imagery draped over the 3D terrain.

Map Zoom & Extent.description: Calculate the geographic extent of the movement tracks and determine an appropriate zoom level and center point for the map. This ensures that all tracks are visible and well-framed when the map is rendered.

pitch.title: Pitch
pitch.description: Tilt of the map in degrees. 0 looks straight down; higher values tilt the view towards the horizon for a 3D look at the terrain. The video cameras use this tilt too.

bearing.title: Bearing
bearing.description: Rotation of the map in degrees clockwise from north. 0 keeps north at the top, 90 puts east at the top, and negative values rotate counter-clockwise. The video cameras use this rotation too.

Animation.description: Control how the tracks animate on the map.

head.title: Marker icon
head.description: Marker drawn at each subject's current position: a flat dot, a preset 3D animal, your own 3D glTF/GLB model, or none.

trips_animation.title: Create Animation
trips_animation.description: Choose the marker shown at each subject's current position as its track plays.

visible.title: Visible
visible.description: Show the playback bar at all.

show_scrubber.title: Show Scrubber
show_scrubber.description: Slider for jumping to any moment.

time_format.title: Time Format
time_format.description: Data time as 'datetime' (2024-01-01 06:00 UTC), 'date', or 'elapsed' since the start.

position.title: Position
position.description: Where the bar sits on the map.

show_camera.title: Show Camera
show_camera.description: Camera button: design and preview the video camera, then copy its settings into render_animation.

create_controls.title: Playback Control
create_controls.description: Choose which playback controls appear on the interactive map, such as play/pause, the time slider and speed buttons, and where they sit.

duration.title: Duration
duration.description: Playback length in seconds (e.g. 30 = the whole timeline plays in 30 seconds).

fps_limit.title: Fps Limit
fps_limit.description: Maximum number of times per second the interactive map redraws while playing. Higher values look smoother but need a faster computer; lower values reduce load on slower machines.

timeline_animation.title: Playback Length & Smoothness
timeline_animation.description: Set how long the animation takes to play from the first location to the last.

Video Export.description: Export the animation as an MP4 video. Video export is off by default, so only the interactive map is produced. Turn on Export video to also create the video.

enabled.title: Export video
enabled.description: Off by default. Turn on to also render the animation as an MP4 video. Exporting a video makes the workflow take longer to run.

camera_settings.title: Camera
camera_settings.description: Camera designed in the interactive map's Camera panel: paste the copied settings, or give the path of the downloaded settings file. The default is a fixed view of the whole scene.

duration.title: Duration
duration.description: Video duration. 'auto' uses the animation's own playback length (duration_s).

overlays.title: Overlays
overlays.description: What the video shows over the map: the date and time, legend, north arrow, scale bar, title and marker labels.

create_animation.title: Video Settings
create_animation.description: Choose how the camera moves, how long the video runs and its resolution.

AnimalModelMarker.description:
A ready-tuned 3D animal model: pick the animal, everything else is preset.

For your own GLB, or to tune orientation/size by hand, use the custom 3D model
(ScenegraphLayerDefinition) instead.

size.description: Multiplier on the preset size (2 = twice as big).
size.title: Size

AnimalModelMarker.title: 3D animal

DotMarker.description:
Flat circle at each subject's current position (deck.gl ScatterplotLayer), filled
with that subject's track colour.

Field names mirror PointLayerStyle. Colours are constants rather than column accessors
because the marker's data is rebuilt in the browser every frame.
DotMarker.title: Dot

NoMarker.description: No marker at the current position; only the trails are drawn.
NoMarker.title: None

ScenegraphLayerDefinition.description:
An animated 3D head built from a glTF/GLB model (deck.gl ScenegraphLayer).

Create one with create_scenegraph_layer() and use it as
TripsAnimation.head. Its position and heading are driven per-frame
from the TripsLayer, so it follows each subject's current location. `glb` accepts
an http(s) URL, a `data:` URI, or a local file path (read and embedded as a data
URI). None -> the preset elephant model. If the ScenegraphLayer
constructor or the glTF loader can't be resolved at runtime, the head silently
falls back to the flat ScatterplotLayer dot. For a ready-tuned animal, use
AnimalModelMarker instead.
See https://deck.gl/docs/api-reference/mesh-layers/scenegraph-layer for more info.

glb.description: GLB source: an http(s) URL, a data: URI, or a local file path. None -> the preset elephant model.
glb.title: 3D model (GLB)

size_scale.description: Model size multiplier. Tune to your scene.
size_scale.title: Size scale

size_min_pixels.description: Clamp the on-screen model to at least this many pixels so it stays visible when zoomed out.
size_min_pixels.title: Min size (px)

size_max_pixels.description: Upper clamp on the model's on-screen size in pixels. Must be at least Min size.
size_max_pixels.title: Max size (px)

face_heading.description: Rotate the model to face its direction of travel.
face_heading.title: Face Heading

yaw_offset.description: Degrees added to the computed heading so the model's nose aligns with travel. Model-dependent; tweak if your model faces sideways.
yaw_offset.title: Yaw Offset

model_pitch.description: Tilt of the MODEL itself (deg), independent of the camera. Use to correct a model authored nose-up/down; NOT the view pitch.
model_pitch.title: Model Pitch

model_roll.description: Bank of the MODEL itself (deg), independent of the camera.
model_roll.title: Model Roll

smooth_samples.description: Heading/slope smoothing window in track fixes (+/- N). Higher = smoother orientation but more lag; 0 = raw single segment.
smooth_samples.title: Smooth Samples

terrain_pitch.description: Tilt the model to the terrain slope (from each fix's z) so it noses up on climbs / down on descents. OFF by default -> stays upright; enable only for steady, climbing tracks (it can tip near-stationary subjects).
terrain_pitch.title: Terrain Pitch

terrain_pitch_scale.description: Sign/strength of terrain pitch. Set -1.0 to flip if the model tilts the wrong way; <1 to soften. (Tilt is also capped at +/-20deg.)
terrain_pitch_scale.title: Terrain Pitch Scale

min_move_m.description: If the subject moves less than this (m) across the smoothing window, hold the last heading and keep the model level -- stops it spinning or tipping while milling in place.
min_move_m.title: Min Move M

pbr_lighting.description: Shade the model with physically-based lighting. Uncheck for flat shading, which shows subject colors more accurately.
pbr_lighting.title: Realistic lighting (PBR)

tint.description: Optional RGB tint over the model as [R, G, B]. None -> the model's own materials.
tint.title: Tint

use_track_color.description: Colour the model with each subject's track colour. False -> use `tint` (or the model's own materials). Note: the colour multiplies the model's material, so it reads truest with a light/neutral glb and flat lighting (pbr_lighting=False).
use_track_color.title: Use subject color

walk_animation.description: Name or index of the model's animation to play while the subject moves (with the trips animation's speed response on). None -> no animation.
walk_animation.title: Walk animation

run_animation.description: Animation played while the subject moves fast (over 2.5x its typical speed). None -> the walk animation.
run_animation.title: Run animation

idle_animation.description: Animation played while the subject rests. None -> the model holds still.
idle_animation.title: Idle animation

animation_speed.description: Playback speed of the model's animations (1 = as authored).
animation_speed.title: Animation Speed

ScenegraphLayerDefinition.title: 3D model (custom)

CameraFromSettings.description: The camera designed in the animated map's Camera panel.

settings.description: Paste the settings copied from the Camera panel, or give the path of the downloaded settings file (.json).
settings.title: Camera settings

CameraFromSettings.title: From Camera panel settings

CameraKeyframe.description:
One waypoint on a keyframes camera path.

Only ``lon``/``lat`` are required. ``t`` places the keyframe on the clip timeline (0 = first
captured frame, 1 = last); when omitted on every keyframe they are spaced evenly.
``zoom``/``pitch``/``bearing`` left as None are interpolated between the nearest keyframes that
define them, or fall back to the whole-scene framing (zoom) and the map's pitch/bearing.

lon.description: Longitude of the camera look-at point.
lon.title: Lon

lat.description: Latitude of the camera look-at point.
lat.title: Lat

t.description: Position on the clip timeline (0 = start, 1 = end). Any increasing numbers work (they are normalized to 0–1); leave blank on every keyframe to space them evenly.
t.title: T

zoom.description: Zoom level at this keyframe. Leave blank to blend from neighbouring keyframes, or fit the whole scene if none set it.
zoom.title: Zoom

pitch.description: Camera tilt in degrees at this keyframe. Leave blank to blend from neighbouring keyframes, or use the map's tilt if none set it.
pitch.title: Pitch

bearing.description: Camera heading in degrees at this keyframe. Leave blank to blend from neighbouring keyframes, or use the map's heading if none set it.
bearing.title: Bearing

CameraKeyframe.title: CameraKeyframe

auto.description: Match the animation's own playback length. Uncheck to set a fixed duration.
auto.title: Auto

seconds.description: Video duration in seconds. Only used when 'Auto' is unchecked.
seconds.title: Duration (seconds)

FixedCamera.description: One view for the whole clip: by default the whole scene, at the map's tilt and heading.

lon.description: Center longitude. Leave blank for the center of the data.
lon.title: Lon

lat.description: Center latitude. Leave blank for the center of the data.
lat.title: Lat

range_m.description: Camera distance from the center in metres. Leave blank to fit the data in the frame.
range_m.title: Range (m)

tilt.description: Tilt in degrees (0 = straight down). Leave blank for the map's.
tilt.title: Tilt

heading.description: Compass heading in degrees. Leave blank for the map's.
heading.title: Heading

fov.description: Vertical lens angle: wider is a wide-angle look, narrower a telephoto one. Leave blank for the map's (about 37°).
fov.title: Field of view (°)

FixedCamera.title: Fixed view

FlyAroundCamera.description:
Fly to a point, then circle it -- the Google Maps 3D flyCameraTo + flyCameraAround pair.

The fly-to follows deck's FlyToInterpolator arc (out, across and back in) from the whole-scene
view; the orbit then turns at a constant rate for `rounds` turns.

lon.description: Center longitude. Leave blank for the center of the data.
lon.title: Lon

lat.description: Center latitude. Leave blank for the center of the data.
lat.title: Lat

range_m.description: Camera distance from the center in metres. Leave blank to fit the data in the frame.
range_m.title: Range (m)

tilt.description: Tilt in degrees (0 = straight down). Leave blank for the map's.
tilt.title: Tilt

heading.description: Compass heading on arrival. Leave blank for the map's.
heading.title: Heading

fov.description: Vertical lens angle: wider is a wide-angle look, narrower a telephoto one. Leave blank for the map's (about 37°).
fov.title: Field of view (°)

fly_frac.description: Share of the clip spent flying in from the whole-scene view. 0 = start at the center.
fly_frac.title: Fly Frac

rounds.description: Full turns around the center after arriving. 0 = hold.
rounds.title: Rounds

FlyAroundCamera.title: Fly to & around

FollowActionCamera.description:
Keeps the moving subjects in frame: frames what animated in the last `follow_window` of the
timeline, re-fitting smoothly as they move and spread.

subjects.description: Only frame these subjects (their value in any column, e.g. names), zooming out as they spread apart. Leave blank for everything that animates.
subjects.title: Subjects

tilt.description: Tilt in degrees (0 = straight down). Leave blank for the map's.
tilt.title: Tilt

heading.description: Compass heading in degrees. Leave blank for the map's.
heading.title: Heading

face_travel.description: Turn the camera to face the direction of travel.
face_travel.title: Face Travel

fov.description: Vertical lens angle: wider is a wide-angle look, narrower a telephoto one. Leave blank for the map's (about 37°).
fov.title: Field of view (°)

follow_window.description: Share of the timeline treated as 'recent' when framing.
follow_window.title: Follow Window

follow_smoothing.description: Share of the gap to the action closed every 1/30 s: low = smooth but laggy, 1 = snaps to it. Independent of fps.
follow_smoothing.title: Follow Smoothing

fit_padding.description: Padding in pixels around the action.
fit_padding.title: Fit Padding

FollowActionCamera.title: Follow the action

FollowSubjectCamera.description:
Stays on one subject at a set range and tilt, behind it and facing where it is heading, lagging a
little behind its moves.

subject.description: Value identifying the subject in any column (e.g. its name or group id). Leave blank for the longest-running track.
subject.title: Subject

range_m.description: Camera distance from the subject in metres.
range_m.title: Range (m)

heading.description: Compass heading in degrees. Leave blank to face the subject's direction of travel.
heading.title: Heading

fov.description: Vertical lens angle: wider is a wide-angle look, narrower a telephoto one. Leave blank for the map's (about 37°).
fov.title: Field of view (°)

follow_smoothing.description: Share of the gap to the subject closed every 1/30 s: low = drifts behind, 1 = locked on.
follow_smoothing.title: Follow Smoothing

turn_smoothing.description: Share of the turn towards the direction of travel made every 1/30 s: low = slow, sweeping turns, 1 = snaps.
turn_smoothing.title: Turn Smoothing

FollowSubjectCamera.title: Follow a subject

KeyframesCamera.description:
Flies through waypoints while the data animates: add views in the Camera panel, upload a
waypoint file, or follow a subject.

Waypoints given in ``keyframes`` take priority over ``source``. Waypoints without a zoom use
the whole-scene framing.

keyframes.description: Camera waypoints, flown through in order. Each needs lon/lat; t (0–1 clip position), zoom, pitch and bearing are optional. Leave empty to build the path from Source instead.
keyframes.title: Keyframes

source.description: How to build the path when `keyframes` is empty: upload a file, or follow a subject.
source.title: Source

keyframe_easing.description: How the camera moves between keyframes: 'smooth' eases in/out of each waypoint, 'linear' moves at constant speed, 'spline' curves through waypoints (Catmull-Rom) without pausing at them.
keyframe_easing.title: Keyframe Easing

fov.description: Vertical lens angle: wider is a wide-angle look, narrower a telephoto one. Leave blank for the map's (about 37°).
fov.title: Field of view (°)

KeyframesCamera.title: Keyframes

KeyframesFromFile.description: Camera path loaded from an uploaded waypoint file.

keyframes_file.description: Path to an uploaded keyframe file: a .json list of {lon, lat, t?, zoom?, pitch?, bearing?} objects, a .geojson of Point features (extras read from properties), or a .csv/.tsv with lon/lat columns. Required for this source.
keyframes_file.title: Keyframes File

KeyframesFromFile.title: Upload waypoint file

KeyframesFromSubject.description:
Camera path auto-derived by following one subject through the animated data.

The subject is matched against every column, so it works for trips and for point or
polygon layers that carry the subject's column.

subject.description: Value identifying the subject in any column (e.g. its name or group id). Leave blank to follow the longest-running track.
subject.title: Subject

KeyframesFromSubject.title: Follow a subject

VideoOverlays.description: What the video shows over the map. The playback bar and camera panel are never shown.

clock.description: The data date and time in a corner, formatted as on the map's playback bar.
clock.title: Clock

clock_position.description: Corner for the date and time.
clock_position.title: Clock Position

title.description: The map title, if it has one.
title.title: Title

labels.description: Labels above the markers (e.g. subject names).
labels.title: Labels

VideoOverlays.title: VideoOverlays
